findings.claim: The `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` docstring says it returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`, but the method now returns `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`.

`MetricAlertDetectorHandler` subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass` and implements none of its abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). Instantiating it through `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler` / `Detector.detector_handler` therefore raises TypeError.

In `test_state_results_multi_group`, the expected occurrence for `group_2` is built with `value=6`, while the data packet has `group_2=10`. The test passes only because the value is not used when the occurrence is constructed.

The test helper `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores its `value` argument and hard-codes the occurrence id, and `IssueOccurrence.__eq__` compares only id. As a result, all mock occurrences compare equal, and tests cannot detect wrong group_key, value or priority passed to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`.
The comment 'TODO: This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction' is stale, because `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler`.

No caller ever passes the `detector_type` parameter of `BaseDetectorHandlerTest.build_handler`. Also, `create_detector_and_conditions(type=None)` replaces None with 'handler_with_state' instead of using a plain default.
The mutable class attribute `counter_names` is not annotated with `typing.ClassVar`.

The new public abstract hook `build_occurrence_and_event_data` has no docstring, unlike its sibling abstract members. It is undocumented that the hook is called only on transitions to non-OK status, that `new_status` arrives as `PriorityLevel`, and that `event_data` is passed unchanged to `produce_occurrence_to_kafka`.
The Kafka publish assertion allows extra publishes, so the test does not catch duplicate occurrence production.
`TestProcessDetectors.setUp` only calls `super().setUp()`, which makes it a no-op override.
